features.feature_value: Pair comparison had little effect; evaluation driven by general freedom-of-speech concern.
features.evidence_span: nothing infulencing how i evaluated the posts as a pair other than that concern.
features.rationale: They explicitly state the pair did not influence their evaluation beyond a freedom-of-speech principle.

features.feature_value: Absolutist First Amendment stance; allow both sides unless harm is involved.
features.evidence_span: unless there’s something that is going to cause physical harm or a threat of harm to someone
features.rationale: They describe a specific threshold (harm/threat) aligned with absolutist speech protection.

features.feature_value: Focus on allowing speech even when it conflicts with personal beliefs; reject only perceived threats/violence.
features.evidence_span: as long as they did not seem like a threat or a possible act of violence, I allowed them.
features.rationale: They tie their decision to perceived threat/violence and emphasize speech even against their beliefs.

features.feature_value: Decision based on whether either post is violent or derogatory.
features.evidence_span: I evaluated at how violent or derogatory either post was.
features.rationale: Their stated evaluation criterion directly targets violence/derogation.

features.feature_value: Swearing alone tolerated; concern is how it is used (e.g., directed at others).
features.evidence_span: Swearing it self wasn't the problem, it was how it was used.
features.rationale: They distinguish profanity from harmful usage, indicating manner/direction as the cue.

features.feature_value: Aiming for balanced evaluation despite viewpoints being far-reaching.
features.evidence_span: ensure it was a balanced evaluation even though most of the viewpoints and context was a bit far reaching.
features.rationale: They describe an approach centered on balance across viewpoints during evaluation.
